title: Case: Recipient on the marathon route asks for a dawn drop or a handover at the barrier
context: A Tallowmere Goods coffee grinder is booked for Sunday morning to an address in Calderwick that lies on the city marathon course. Dispatch owns bookings.
initial_request: Just seen the marathon thing. Can the driver come at 6am before they shut the road? Or just bring it at 8 like it's booked and I'll walk out to the barrier on Mill Quay and grab it off him. I'm out from 1pm Sunday until late so the afternoon's no use to me.

events.to: All partner desks; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: SERVICE NOTICE SN-4035. Calderwick Marathon, Sunday 17 October. The council closes the course roads 05:30–13:30 UTC, including Wharfside Terrace, Mill Quay and Tanner's Row. No Ashgrove Arc vehicle will enter the course while it is closed. Drivers will not make pre-closure drops before their route start or hand parcels over at barriers. Morning bookings on affected streets will be re-offered by Dispatch. Partner desks: do not raise traces for parcels held under this notice.

DL-7467 (TG-2599, coffee grinder) for Hesper Yardley, 9 Wharfside Terrace, is booked Sunday 17 October 7:00–11:00 UTC and falls under SN-4035. We can offer Sunday 17 October 14:00–18:00 or Monday 18 October 8:00–12:00, no charge. Nothing will be moved until the recipient chooses.

events.from: Rosalind Kinsella, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the driver told me DL-7467 was handed to someone at the door, so it's been delivered.

Just seen the marathon thing. Can the driver come at 6am before they shut the road? Or just bring it at 8 like it's booked and I'll walk out to the barrier on Mill Quay and grab it off him. I'm out from 1pm Sunday until late so the afternoon's no use to me.

acceptable_actions.summary: Explain that a 06:00 drop and a barrier handover are not available under Ashgrove Arc's marathon notice, offer the Dispatch-confirmed alternatives (Monday 18 October 8:00–12:00, or Sunday 15:00–18:00, which she says she cannot do) and ask her to choose before anything is booked.

Explain that a 06:00 drop and a barrier handover are not available under Ashgrove Arc's marathon notice, offer the Dispatch-confirmed alternatives (Monday 18 October 8:00–12:00, or Sunday 15:00–18:00, which she says she cannot do) and ask her to choose before anything is booked. (by Email, the channel the escalation arrived on)

must: Replies to Hesper Yardley on the Customer portal about DL-7467.
Says the carrier will not make a pre-closure 06:00 drop or hand the parcel over at the barrier while the course is closed.
Offers the slots Dispatch has offered (Monday 18 October 8:00–12:00 UTC, and Sunday 15:00–18:00 UTC) and asks her to choose, noting the Monday slot given she is out on Sunday afternoon.
must_not: Says the delivery has been moved or booked to any slot before she has chosen and Dispatch has confirmed it.
Asks Dispatch to run a 06:00 drop or a barrier handover, or tells the recipient either might be arranged.
Promises an exact arrival time within a slot.
Raises a trace or investigation for a parcel held under the service notice.
Treats the claim from Rosalind Kinsella (who has no recorded link to DL-7467) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Rosalind Kinsella's message
expected.reference_message: Hi Hesper, thanks for getting in touch. Because of the marathon, Wharfside Terrace and Mill Quay are closed on Sunday morning, and Ashgrove Arc has said its drivers won't make early drops before the closure or hand parcels over at the barriers. So I can't arrange either of those. Dispatch has offered two other slots at no charge: Monday 18 October 8:00–12:00 UTC, or Sunday 17 October 14:00–18:00 UTC. As you're out on Sunday afternoon, Monday morning may suit you better. Tell me which you'd like and I'll ask Dispatch to book it. Nothing changes until they confirm.

rationale: Rule-made from city-021: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The escalation arrives by Email instead of Customer portal; replying on either channel is accepted. An unverified bystander, Rosalind Kinsella, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
